(p-469) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-An'am

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. Regarding His saying ﴿ya'diluna﴾ (ascribe equals), scholars have two interpretations:

The first: it derives from *al-'udul* ('an al-shay'), meaning deviation and turning away from something. On this view, *bi-rabbihim* (to their Lord) is connected to *kafaru* (disbelieved), and the meaning is: those who disbelieve in their Lord turn aside and deviate from the path of truth into disbelief and error. It has also been said on this interpretation that the *ba'* (bi-) has the meaning of *'an* (from), i.e., they turn away from their Lord, so they do not direct themselves to Him in obedience or faith.

The second: the *ba'* is connected to *ya'diluna*, and the meaning of *ya'diluna* is that they make for Him a counterpart in worship. This is from the Arabic usage: "I equated so-and-so with so-and-so" (*'adaltu fulanan bi-fulan*) when I made him a counterpart and equal. From this is the saying of Jarir:

*Do you equate the Tha'labah of the horsemen, or the Riyah, with Tuhayyah and al-Khishab?*

He means: did you make Tuhayyah and al-Khishab equals and peers of the Banu Tha'labah and the Banu Riyah? This last interpretation is supported by the Qur'an, such as His saying, concerning the disbelievers who equated others with Him: ﴿By Allah, we were indeed in clear error, when we equated you with the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 97-98]. And His saying: ﴿Among people are those who take others besides Allah as rivals, loving them as they love Allah﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165]. He, Exalted is He, has indicated in many verses that the disbelievers made the created equal to the Creator, may Allah disfigure them, such as His saying: ﴿Or have they ascribed to Allah partners who created as He creates, so that the creation seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Subduer﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16]; and His saying: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who creates not? Will you not remember?﴾ [al-Nahl: 17]; and His saying: ﴿He presents to you an example from yourselves: Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided you, so that you are equal therein?﴾ [al-Rum: 28], and other verses besides these.

In the language, *'idl* (equal) of a thing is its like and its counterpart. Some scholars of Arabic said: if it is of the same kind, it is *'idl* with a kasra on the ayn; if it is not of the same kind, it is *'adl* with a fatha on the ayn. From the first is the saying of Muhalhil:

*That there is no equal of Kulayb (in him) when the veiled women are unveiled*

*That there is no equal of Kulayb when the 'idah trees are stirred by the south wind*

*That there is no equal of Kulayb on the morning of the great calamity's tumult*

He means that the slain whom the Banu Bakr ibn Wa'il killed in revenge for their brother Kulayb, who was killed by Jassas ibn Murrah al-Bakri, are not equal to him, nor are they his peers in nobility.

From the second is His saying: ﴿or its equivalent in fasting﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95], because what is meant is the counterpart of the food-feeding in fasting, which is not of its kind. And His saying: ﴿And if they offer every ransom (*'adl*)﴾ [al-An'am: 70]; and His saying: ﴿nor will any ransom (*'adl*) be accepted from it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123]. *'Adl* here means ransom, because it is as if it were an equivalent value set against the ransom, taken in its place.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth; He knows your secret and your open﴾ [al-An'am: 3]. In this noble verse there are three interpretations among the scholars of tafsir, and each of them has a witness in the Book of Allah, Exalted is He:

The first: the meaning is ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth﴾, i.e., He is the God who is worshipped in the heavens and on the earth, because He, Majestic and Exalted, is alone the one truly worshipped in the earth and the heaven. On this view, the clause *ya'lamu* (He knows) is a circumstantial clause (*hal*) or a predicate (*khabar*). This meaning is clarified and witnessed by His saying: ﴿And He is the One who is God in the heaven and God on the earth﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 84], i.e., He is the one truly worshipped in the heaven and the earth. The worship of the disbelievers of other than Him carries no weight, for it is a burden upon them, by which they abide forever in the Fire, an everlasting abiding. Their objects of worship are not partners with Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He above that by a great exaltation: ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority﴾ [al-Najm: 23]. And His saying: ﴿And those who call upon other than Allah as partners follow nothing but conjecture, and they only guess﴾ [Yunus: 66].

This view on the verse is the most apparent of the views, and al-Qurtubi chose it.

The second: His saying ﴿in the heavens and on the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 3] is connected to His saying ﴿He knows your secret﴾, i.e., He is Allah who knows your secret in the heavens and on the earth. This view is explained and witnessed by His saying: ﴿Say: He sent it down who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Furqan: 6].

Al-Nahhas said: this view is among the best of what has been said about the verse; al-Qurtubi transmitted it from him.

The third, which is the choice of Ibn Jarir: the pause is complete at His saying *fi al-samawat* (in the heavens), and His saying *wa fi al-ardh* (and on the earth) is connected to what follows, i.e., He knows your secret and your open in the earth. The meaning of this view is that He, Majestic and Exalted, is established upon His Throne above all His creation, while He knows the secret and the open of the people of the earth; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

This view is clarified and witnessed by His saying: ﴿Are you secure from He who is in the heaven, that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and then it shakes?﴾ ﴿Or are you secure from He who is in the heaven, that He will not send upon you a violent wind?﴾ [al-Mulk: 16-17]; and His saying: ﴿The Most Merciful is established upon the Throne﴾ [Ta-Ha: 5], together with His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]; and His saying: ﴿Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ [al-A'raf: 7]. The verification of this matter will come, Allah willing, with clarification in Surah al-A'raf. Know that what the Jahmiyyah (a sect that denied Allah's attributes) claim, that Allah, Exalted is He, is in every place, citing this verse as evidence that He is in the earth, is manifest error and ignorance of Allah, Exalted is He. For all existing places are far too lowly and too small for the Lord of the heavens and the earth to dwell in any of them, He who is greater than everything and higher than everything, encompassing everything, and nothing encompasses Him. The heavens and the earth in His hand, Majestic and Exalted is He, are smaller than a grain of mustard seed in the hand of any one of us, and His is the highest description. If a grain of mustard seed were in a man's hand, can it be said that he is indwelling in it, or in every part of it? No, and never; it is smaller and more insignificant than that. Knowing this, know that the Lord of the heavens and the earth is greater than everything and mightier than everything, encompassing everything, and nothing encompasses Him, and nothing is above Him: ﴿Not an atom's weight is hidden from Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor is anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear record﴾ [Saba': 3]. Glorified and Exalted is He by a great exaltation; we cannot count the praise of Him. He is as He praised Himself: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, while they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a Book written on parchment, and they had touched it with their hands, those who disbelieved would have said, "This is nothing but manifest magic."﴾

In this noble verse, He mentions that if God had sent down to the disbelievers a written book on *qirtas* (parchment, meaning a sheet or scroll), in response to what they had proposed, as He said of them: ﴿And we will never believe in you until you cause a book to descend upon us that we can read﴾ [al-Isra': 93], and they then witnessed that descending book and their hands touched it, they would have persisted in their obstinacy and claimed that it was due to magic that had bewitched them. This stubbornness, great contentiousness, and arrogant denial, which is the characteristic of the disbelievers, He explained in many verses, such as His saying: (p-472) ﴿And even if We opened for them a gate from the heaven and they continued to ascend through it﴾ ﴿they would surely say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled; rather, we are a people bewitched."﴾ [al-Hijr: 14, 15].

• And His saying: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, "It is layered clouds."﴾ [al-Tur: 44],

• And His saying: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and made the dead speak to them and gathered against them every thing before them, they would not have believed unless God willed﴾ [al-An'am: 111],

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been decreed will not believe.﴾ ﴿Even if every sign should come to them﴾ [Yunus: 96, 97],

• And His saying: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101],

• And His saying: ﴿And if they should see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾ [al-A'raf: 146], along with other verses. He also mentioned a similar obstinacy and contentiousness regarding Pharaoh and his people in His saying: ﴿And they said, "Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with it, we will not be believers in you."﴾ [al-A'raf: 132].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why was an angel not sent down to him?"﴾ Here he does not clarify what they mean by sending down the angel they proposed. However, he makes it clear in another place that they wanted the angel to be another warner alongside the Prophet (ﷺ). This is in His saying: ﴿And they say, "What is this messenger that he eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him so that he could be a warner with him?"﴾ [al-Furqan: 7], to the end of the verse.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.﴾ He means: if He had sent down the angels to them while they were in their state of disbelief and sins, the punishment would have come to them from Allah without any delay or respite. This is because He has decreed that the angels do not descend upon them except with that (i.e., with the punishment), as He clarified by His saying: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be given respite﴾ [al-Hijr: 8], and His saying: ﴿On the day they see the angels, there will be no good news that day for the criminals﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Furqan: 22].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have obscured for them what they obscure.﴾ That is: if We had sent to mankind an angelic messenger, he would have been in the form of a man, so that they could address him and benefit by taking knowledge from him, because they would not be able to look at the angels due to the intensity of their light. And if he were so, the matter would have been confused for them, just as they confuse matters for themselves in accepting the message of a human messenger.

This noble verse indicates that the messenger ought to be of the same kind as those to whom he is sent, as Allah, may He be exalted, also indicated with His saying: ﴿Say: If there were in the earth angels walking securely, We would certainly have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ [al-Isra': 95].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but there beset those who mocked them of that which they used to mock.﴾ (p-473) In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, mentions that the disbelievers mocked messengers before our Prophet ﷺ, and that the punishment befell them because of that. He does not detail here the manner of their mockery, nor the manner of the punishment by which they were destroyed. But He has elaborated much of that in many other places: in the mention of Nuh (Noah) and his people, Hud and his people, Salih and his people, Lut (Lot) and his people, Shu'ayb and his people, and beyond that.

From their mockery of Nuh is their saying to him: "After you were a prophet, you have become a carpenter." Allah, may He be exalted, said of Nuh: ﴿If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock﴾ [Hud: 38], and He mentioned what befell them with His saying: ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hujurat: 14], and similar verses.

From their mockery of Hud is what Allah related of them: ﴿We say nothing except that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ [Hud: 54], and His saying about them also: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear evidence, and we will not leave our gods on your say-so"﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 53]. He mentioned the punishment that befell them in His saying: ﴿We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Dhariyat: 41], and similar verses.

From their mockery of Salih is their saying, as Allah related of them: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 77], and their saying: ﴿O Salih, you were among us a hope before this﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 62]. He mentioned what befell them with His saying: ﴿And the cry seized those who did wrong, so they became in their homes fallen prostrate﴾ [Hud: 94], and similar verses.

From their mockery of Lut is their saying, as Allah related of them: ﴿The answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel the family of Lut from your town"﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Naml: 56], and their saying to him also: ﴿If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be among those expelled﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 167]. He mentioned what befell them with His saying: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon them stones of baked clay﴾ [al-Hijr: 74], and similar verses.

From their mockery of Shu'ayb is their saying, as Allah related of them: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and we see you among us as weak; and were it not for your tribe, we would have stoned you, and you are not over us mighty"﴾ [Hud: 91]. He mentioned what befell them with His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them; indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 189], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾. He means: He, exalted is He, is the One who provides sustenance to the creatures, and He is the absolutely Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani al-Mutlaq), so He has no need of sustenance. Allah, exalted is He, has made this clear in His saying: (p-474) ﴿I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want that they should feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 56, 57, 58]. The reading of the majority is that both verbs are from the causative form (al-ikham, "to feed"): the first is in the active voice and the second is in the passive voice, as we have explained, and as another verse makes clear. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid and al-A'mash read the first verb as the majority does, and the second with a fatha on the ya' and the 'ayn, as the present tense of the triliteral ta'ima (to eat), whose past tense has a kasra on the 'ayn; that is, He provides for His servants and feeds them, while He, majestic and exalted is He, does not eat, because He has no need of what the created being needs of food. For He, majestic and exalted, is self-sufficient in His essence, the absolutely Self-Sufficient, glorified and exalted far above that by a great exaltation. ﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah, and Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15].

The reading we mentioned from Sa'id, Mujahid and al-A'mash agrees with one of the opinions regarding the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge (as-Samad)﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 2]. Some scholars said: as-Samad is the master (as-sayyid) to whom one turns in times of hardship and needs. Others said: he is the master whose lordship, nobility, greatness, knowledge and wisdom are perfected. Others said: as-Samad is He who neither begets nor is begotten, and none is equal to Him; and according to this, what follows is an explanation of it. Others said: he is the One who remains after the annihilation of His creation. Others said: as-Samad is the One who has no hollow (jawf) and does not eat food, and this is the point of evidence. Among those who held this view were Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Mujahid, Abdullah ibn Buraydah, Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi, as Ibn Kathir and Ibn Jarir and others have transmitted from them.

The author of these notes, may Allah pardon him, says: It is well known in the speech of the Arabs to apply as-samad to the great master, and to a solid thing that has no hollow. Of the first is the saying of az-Zibriqan:

"Travel together at midnight and make haste, and there is no hostage except a master, samad."

And the saying of another:

"I struck him with a sword, then I said to him: take it, Hudhayf, for you are the master, the samad."

And the saying of another:

"Has the herald not come early with the best of the Banu Asad, with 'Amr ibn Mas'ud and with the master, the samad?"

And of the second is the saying of the poet:

"A flame of wars whose horses never cease, grim, chewing the bit, made firm (al-musammad)."

When you know this, Allah, exalted is He, is the Master to whom alone one turns in hardships and needs, and He is the One who is far removed from and exalted above the attributes of created beings, such as eating food and the like, glorified and exalted far above that by a great exaltation.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾ — the verse — He means: the first of those who submit from this nation to which I was sent, and it is not meant to be the first of all people to submit, as He has made clear in many verses that indicate the existence of Muslims before his existence ﷺ and the existence of his nation,

- like His saying about Abraham: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 131];
- and His saying about Joseph: ﴿Take me in death as a Muslim and join me with the righteous﴾ [Yusuf: 101];
- and His saying: ﴿By which the prophets who submitted judge﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44];
- and His saying about Lot and his family: ﴿We found not in it any house other than of the Muslims﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 36];

along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him; and if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent﴾. By His saying here, ﴿then He is over all things competent﴾ [al-An'am: 17], after His saying ﴿and if He touches you with good﴾, He indicates that His bounty and His abundant giving cannot be turned back by anyone from whomever He wills it for, as He stated explicitly in His saying: ﴿And if He intends for you good, there is none who can repel His bounty; He causes it to reach whom He wills﴾ [Yunus: 107], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾. In this noble verse He declares that he (ﷺ) is a warner to everyone whom this mighty Qur'an reaches, whoever they may be. It is understood from the verse that the warning by it is general to everyone it reaches, and that everyone it reaches and who does not believe in it is in the Fire, and this is so.

As for the generality of his warning to everyone it reaches, other verses also indicate it, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158],

• and His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28],

• and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His Servant that he may be to the worlds a warner﴾ [al-Furqan: 1].

As for the entry into the Fire of whoever does not believe in it, He has declared it, exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

As for whoever the call of the Messenger (ﷺ) has not reached, he has the ruling of the people of the fatrah (the interval between prophets) to whom no messenger came, and Allah knows best.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾. This noble verse indicates that Allah, the Exalted, whose knowledge encompasses every existent and non-existent thing, knows the non-existent, which He has known from eternity (al-azal) would not occur, and how it would be if it did occur. This is because He knows that the return of the disbelievers to the worldly life a second time on the Day of Resurrection will not happen, and He knows how this return, which will not happen, would be if it did occur. He stated this in His words: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly go back to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. This meaning is also stated explicitly in other verses.

Among them is that He, the Exalted, knew from eternity that the hypocrites who stayed behind from the expedition of Tabuk would not go out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Allah held them back from it for a wisdom, as He stated in His words: ﴿But Allah disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Tawbah: 46]. He knows that this going out, which would not occur, how it would be if it did occur, as Allah, the Exalted, stated in His words: ﴿If they had gone out among you, they would have increased you in nothing but corruption﴾, up to the end of the verse [al-Tawbah: 47]. Among the verses indicating the meaning mentioned is His words, the Exalted: ﴿And if We had mercy on them and removed what afflicts them of adversity, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 75], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 33:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾ – the verse – in this noble verse Allah, the Exalted, declares explicitly that He knows that His Messenger (ﷺ) is grieved by what the disbelievers say in denying him (ﷺ). Allah, the Exalted, has forbidden this excessive grief in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿So let not your soul go out in grief over them﴾ – the verse [Fatir: 8],

• and His saying: ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 68],

• and His saying: ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces, if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow﴾ [al-Kahf: 6],

• and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself, [in grief] that they will not be believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3].

Al-ba'ikh (الباخع) is the one who destroys himself. From this is the saying of Ghaylan ibn 'Uqbah:

[Al-Tawil]

Ah, O you who destroy himself through grief,
for a thing the decrees have snatched from his hands.

His saying, ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself﴾, in the two verses, is intended as a prohibition against that. Its parallel is: ﴿Perhaps you would leave aside some of what is revealed to you﴾ [Hud: 12], meaning: do not destroy yourself with grief over them in the first, and do not leave aside some of what is revealed to you in the second.

(p. 477) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [the verse].

The majority of the scholars of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) said: What is meant by "the dead" in this verse is the disbelievers. Several verses of the Book of Allah support this, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾ [the verse] [al-An'am: 122],

• and His saying: ﴿The living and the dead are not alike﴾ [Fatir: 22],

• and His saying: ﴿You cannot make those in the graves hear﴾ [Fatir: 22],

along with other verses.

The Qur'anic verse: ﴿Say: Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.﴾

He mentions in this noble verse that He is able to send down the sign that the disbelievers demanded of His Messenger, and He indicates the wisdom behind not sending it down with His words: ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ [al-An'am: 37]. In another place He explains that the wisdom behind not sending it down is that, if it were sent down and they did not believe in it, the immediate punishment would descend upon them, as happened to the people of Salih when they demanded of him that he bring forth from a solid rock a she-camel, pregnant in her tenth month, healthy and hollow-bodied. Allah brought it forth for them from it by His power and will, but they slaughtered her. ﴿And they said, "O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with"﴾ [al-A'raf: 77]. Allah then destroyed them all at once with a punishment of total annihilation (ʿadhāb al-istiʾṣāl, a punishment that uproots a people entirely). This is in His words: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a warning﴾ [al-Isra': 59].

He explains in other places that there is no need for the signs they demanded, because He has sent down to them a sign greater than all the signs they demanded and others besides, and that sign is this great Qur'an. This is in His words: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 51]. His, glorified and exalted is He, denunciation of them for not being content with this Book in place of the demanded signs indicates that it is greater and more magnificent than every sign. And so it is. Do you not see that it is a clear sign and a dazzling miracle, which has overwhelmed all the people of the earth, and it remains, echoing in the ears of creation, fresh and tender, until the command of Allah comes? This is unlike the other miracles of the Messengers, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them, for all of them have passed and ended.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful? Nay, it is Him alone you call upon﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, mentions that when a punishment from Allah comes upon the polytheists, or the Hour comes upon them, they sincerely direct their supplication (du'a', which is the marrow of worship) to Allah alone, and forget what they used to associate with Him, because they know that none removes distresses except Allah alone, exalted and high is He.

Here He did not specify the type of worldly punishment that compels them to sincerity toward Allah, nor did He specify here whether, when He removes the punishment from them, they continue in their sincerity or return to their disbelief and polytheism. However, He explained all of that in other places.

He explained that the worldly punishment that compels them to sincerity is the descent of distresses by which the one upon whom they descend fears destruction, such as the sea rising against them and its waves crashing, and it becomes their assumption that they will drown in it unless they sincerely direct their supplication to Allah alone,

such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice therein, there comes upon them a stormy wind, and the waves come upon them from every place, and they assume that they have been encompassed, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion: "If You save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful." But when He saves them, behold, they commit injustice in the earth without right﴾ [Yunus: 22, 23],

and His saying: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him﴾ [al-Isra': 67],

and His saying: ﴿So when they board ships, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 65],

and His saying: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Luqman: 32],

along with other verses.

He also explained that when Allah removes that distress from them, they return to what they were upon of polytheism, in many places,

such as His saying: ﴿So when He delivers you to the land, you turn away, and man is ever ungrateful﴾,

and His saying: ﴿So when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate partners﴾,

and His saying: ﴿Say: Allah delivers you from it and from every distress; then you associate partners﴾ [al-An'am: 64],

and His saying: ﴿But when He saves them, behold, they commit injustice in the earth without right﴾, along with other verses.

He, exalted is He, also explained that their return to polytheism after Allah had saved them from drowning is due to the intensity of their ignorance and blindness, because He is able to destroy them on land just as He is able to destroy them at sea, and He is able to return them to the sea another time and destroy them there by drowning. Therefore their audacity toward Him when they reach land has no justification, since it stems from their ignorance and misguidance. This is in His saying: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a squall of stones, then you will not find for yourselves a protector? Or do you feel secure that He will not return you into it another time and send against you a storm of wind and drown you for what you disbelieved, then you will not find for yourselves against Us any avenger?﴾ [al-Isra': 68, 69].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 52:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾. In this noble verse, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade His Prophet ﷺ from driving away the weak among the Muslims and their poor, those who call upon their Lord morning and evening seeking His countenance. In another verse He commanded him to restrain himself to remain with them, and not to let his eyes turn away from them toward the people of rank and station in this world, and He forbade him from obeying the disbelievers in that matter, namely His saying:

(p-479) ﴿And restrain yourself to remain with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance. And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life. And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his own desire and whose affair has been [ever] neglect﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. Just as He commanded him here to give them the greeting of peace and to give them the good news of the mercy of their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, in His saying:

﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: "Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed upon Himself mercy"﴾ [al-An'am: 54], to the end of the verse. And He made clear in other verses that the driving away of the weak among the Muslims, which the disbelieving Arabs demanded of our Prophet ﷺ, and so Allah forbade him from it, was also demanded of Noah by the people of Noah, and he refused:

• As in His saying, may He be exalted, concerning him: ﴿And I am not one to drive away those who have believed﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 29],

• And His saying: ﴿And O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I drove them away?﴾ to the end of the verse [Hud: 30],

• And His saying: ﴿And I am not one to drive away the believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 114]. This is from the resemblance of the hearts of the disbelievers mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Their hearts have resembled one another﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Baqarah: 118].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus did We test some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?" Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ Allah, exalted is He, has ordained as a matter of wisdom that most of the followers of the Messengers are the weak among people. For this reason, when Heraclius, the king of the Romans, asked Abu Sufyan about our Prophet (ﷺ): "Do the nobles of the people follow him, or are they the weak among them?" He said: "Rather, the weak among them." He said: "They are the followers of the Messengers."

Having understood this, know that He, exalted is He, indicated that among the wisdom in this is the trial of some people by means of others. The people of standing, nobility and rank say: "If there were any good in this religion, these would not have preceded us to it, for we are more deserving of every good than they are." As He said here: ﴿And thus did We test some of them by means of others, that they might say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾ and so on [al-An'am: 53], in denial on their part that Allah should bestow favour upon these weak ones rather than them, supposing that they themselves are more deserving of good than they are. Allah has refuted their saying here with His words: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾

This meaning has been clarified in other verses, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Had it been good, they would not have preceded us to it"﴾ and so on [al-Ahqaf: 11], and His saying: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of the two groups is better in position and finer in assembly?"﴾ [Maryam: 73].

The meaning is: when they saw themselves in better dwellings and comfort than the weak among the Muslims, they believed that they were more entitled than them to every good, and that following the Messenger (ﷺ) would not have been good, had it been good, they would not have preceded them to it. Allah refuted this fabrication of theirs with His saying: ﴿And how many generations before them did We destroy, who were better in furnishing and appearance?﴾ [Maryam: 74], and His saying: ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is us hastening to them with good? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 55-56], along with other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 57:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Not with me is what you seek to hasten﴾ and so on. In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to inform the disbelievers that the hastening of the punishment upon them, which they ask him for, is not with him; rather it is with Allah. If He wills, He hastens it, and if He wills, He delays it from them. Then He commanded him to tell them that if it were with him, he would hasten it upon them, by His saying: ﴿Say: If what you seek to hasten were with me, the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾ and so on [al-An'am: 58].

He made clear in other places that what moved them to seek the hastening of the punishment was nothing but disbelief and denial, and that if they were to witness that punishment they would know that it is great and terrifying, and that none would seek to hasten it except an ignorant person like them,

such as His saying: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them for a counted community, they will surely say: What holds it back? Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them, and what they used to mock will surround them﴾ [Hud: 8],

and His saying: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are fearful of it﴾ and so on [al-Shura: 54],

and His saying: ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed Hell will surround the disbelievers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 54],

and His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if His punishment came to you by night or by day, what part of it would the criminals seek to hasten?﴾ [Yunus: 50].

He made clear in another place that, were it not that Allah had set for them a term before which the punishment would not come to them, He would have hastened it upon them. This is His saying: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment; and were it not for a specified term, it would have come to them﴾ and so on [al-'Ankabut: 53].

Note (tanbih)

His saying, the Exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Say: If what you seek to hasten were with me, the matter would have been decided﴾ and so on, is explicit that if the hastening of the punishment upon them were in his hand, he would have hastened it upon them. Yet it is established in the "Two Sahihs" from the hadith of 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) — Allah sent to him the angel of the mountains, and said to him: "If you wish, I will close the two mountains (al-Akhshabayn) upon them, and they are the two mountains of Makkah that flank it." So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins those who worship Allah and associate nothing with Him."

The apparent answer is what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, gave in his tafsir of this verse, namely: this verse indicates that if the occurrence of the punishment they seek to hasten were in his power at the time they ask for it, he would have hastened it upon them. As for the hadith, there is nothing in it that they sought the hastening of the punishment at that time; rather the angel offered him their destruction and he chose not to destroy them. The difference between the obstinate one who seeks the hastening of the punishment and others is not hidden.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am 6:59]. He, exalted is He, clarified what is meant by "the keys of the unseen" in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain, and He knows what is in the wombs. No soul knows what it will earn tomorrow, and no soul knows in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [Luqman 31:34]. Al-Bukhari, Ahmad, and others narrated from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that what is meant by "the keys of the unseen" are the five mentioned in that verse. The word "mafatih" (keys) is the plural of "mafkhar" with a fatha on the mim, meaning a treasury (makhzan). It has also been said that it is "mafatih," the plural of "miftah" with a kasra on the mim, meaning the key itself, and the recitation of Ibn al-Sumayq supports this. In his recitation it is "mafatiyh," with a ya' after the ta', the plural of "miftah."

This noble verse indicates that none knows the unseen except Allah, and this is so, because creatures know nothing except what their Creator, majestic and exalted, has taught them.

Also, 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Whoever claims that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) knows what will happen tomorrow has indeed greatly slandered Allah." And Allah says: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [al-Naml 27:65]. Narrated by Muslim. In this noble surah, Allah commanded him (ﷺ) to announce to the people that he does not know the unseen, and that is in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me﴾ [al-An'am 6:50].

For this reason, when 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) was accused of the slander (al-ifk), he did not know whether she was innocent or not, until Allah informed him by His saying: ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾ [al-Nur 24:26].

Ibrahim (peace be upon him and our Prophet) slaughtered his calf for the angels, and he had no knowledge that they were angels until they informed him and said to him: ﴿Indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lut﴾ [Hud 11:70]. When they came to Lut, he also did not know that they were angels; therefore ﴿he was distressed for them and felt helpless for them, and said, "This is a difficult day"﴾ [Hud 11:77], fearing for them that his people would commit upon them their well-known indecency, until he said: ﴿If only I had against you some power, or could take refuge in a strong support﴾ [Hud 11:80]. He did not know their news until they said to him: ﴿Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you﴾ and the verses that follow [Hud 11:81].

And Ya'qub (peace be upon him): his eyes became white from grief over Yusuf, while he was in Egypt, not knowing his news, until Allah revealed the news of Yusuf.

And Sulayman (peace be upon him), although Allah subjected the devils and the wind to him, did not know about the people of Ma'rib, the people of Bilqis, until the hoopoe came to him and said to him: ﴿I have encompassed that which you have not encompassed, and I have come to you from Sheba with certain news﴾ and the verses that follow [al-Naml 27:22].

And Nuh (peace be upon him and our Prophet): he did not know that his son who drowned was not of his family, those promised salvation, until he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true﴾ and the verse [Hud 11:45]. He did not know the reality of the matter until Allah informed him by His saying: ﴿He said, "O Nuh, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is one whose work is other than righteous. So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be among the ignorant"﴾ [Hud 11:46].

Allah, exalted, has said concerning Nuh in Surah Hud: ﴿And I do not say to you that with me are the treasures of Allah, nor do I know the unseen﴾ and the verse [al-An'am 6:50]. As for the angels (upon them be blessings and peace), when He said to them: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.﴾ ﴿They said, "Exalted are You; we have no knowledge except what You have taught us"﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:31-32].

It is thus clear that the most knowledgeable of creatures, who are the messengers, and the angels, know of the unseen only what Allah, exalted, has taught them. He, exalted, teaches His messengers from His unseen what He wills, as He indicated by His saying: ﴿And Allah would not inform you of the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:179], and His saying: ﴿[He is] the Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to one whom He has approved of the messengers﴾ and the verse [al-Jinn 72:26-27].

Caution

When the Great Qur'an came with the statement that none knows the unseen except Allah, all the means by which one seeks to reach some knowledge of the unseen, other than revelation, became clear misguidance, and some of them amount to disbelief.

For this reason it is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever goes to an 'arraf (fortune-teller) and asks him about something, his prayer will not be accepted for forty days." There is no disagreement among the scholars on the prohibition of 'iyafah (augury by birds), kahanah (soothsaying), 'arafah (fortune-telling), tarq (geomancy/pebble-casting), zajr (omen-reading), and astrology, and all of these fall under kahanah, because it includes all kinds of claiming to have insight into the knowledge of the unseen.

And the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about soothsayers (kuhhan), and he said: "They are nothing."

(p-483) Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse, and his exact words are: Whoever says that rain will fall tomorrow and asserts it, is a disbeliever, whether he reports it based on a sign he claims or not. Likewise, whoever says that he knows what is in the womb is a disbeliever. But if he does not assert it, and says that the nawʾ (star-rising) customarily brings down water, and that it is a customary cause of water, and that it is a cause of water in accordance with what Allah has decreed and what has preceded in His knowledge, he does not disbelieve. However, it is recommended for him not to speak of it, for in it there is a resemblance to the words of the people of disbelief, and ignorance of His subtle wisdom, since He sends rain whenever He wills, sometimes with a particular nawʾ and sometimes without a nawʾ.

Allah, exalted, has said: "There has become among My servants one who believes in Me and one who disbelieves in the stars," as will be explained in its place in the narration, if Allah wills.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: Likewise is the saying of the physician that if the right breast's nipple is darkened, the child is male, and if it is on the left breast, it is female; and if the woman finds the right side heavier, the child is female. If one claims this as a customary matter and not as a necessary fact of creation, he does not disbelieve, nor does he become a sinner.

As for one who claims the earning of the future of one's life, he is a disbeliever; or who reports about the events, general or detailed, before they happen, there is no doubt of his disbelief as well. As for one who reports about the eclipses of the sun and the moon, our scholars said: he is disciplined but not imprisoned. As for not declaring him a disbeliever, it is because a group said that this is a matter known through calculation and the determination of the stations, as Allah reported in His saying: ﴿And the moon—We have determined for it stations﴾ [Ya Sin 36:39].

As for their being disciplined, it is because they introduce doubt among the common people, who do not know the difference between this and other matters, so they confuse their beliefs and abandon their foundations of certainty. Therefore they are disciplined, so that they conceal it if they know it and do not announce it.

I say: Among this category is what came in Sahih Muslim from one of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ): that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes to an 'arraf and asks him about something, his prayer will not be accepted for forty nights." The 'arraf is the diviner and astrologer who claims knowledge of the unseen, and this practice is 'arafah, and its practitioner is an 'arraf. He is one who infers matters from causes and premises he claims to know. Some practitioners of this art support this with zajr, tarq, astrology, and customary causes of that sort. This art is 'iyafah with a ya', and all of these are covered by the name kahanah, as al-Qadi 'Iyad said.

Kahanah is the claim to knowledge of the unseen.

Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr said in al-Kafi: Among the earnings whose prohibition is agreed upon are usury, the wages of prostitutes, illicit gain, bribery, taking pay for wailing and singing, for soothsaying and claiming the unseen and news of the sky, for flutes and play, and all falsehood. End of quotation from al-Qurtubi in his words, and I have seen his definition of the 'arraf and the kahin.

Al-Baghawi said: The 'arraf is one who claims knowledge of matters by premises through which he infers the stolen, the place of the lost, and the like. Abu al-'Abbas ibn Taymiyyah said: 'Arraf is a name for the kahin, the astrologer, the sand-diviner, and similar ones who speak about knowledge of matters by these means.

As for tarq: it is said to be the line (khatt) by which one claims insight into the unseen. It is also said to be the casting of pebbles which women do. Zajr is 'iyafah, which is the seeking of omens of ill or good luck from birds, and claiming knowledge of matters from the manner of their flight, their places, their names, their colors, and the directions toward which they fly.

From this is the saying of 'Alqamah ibn 'Abdah al-Tamimi:

*Whoever crosses the path of the ravens, seeking to drive them away for his own safety, will surely be met with ill omen.*

The Banu Lahab were the most skilled of the Arabs in 'iyafah, until a poet said about them:

*The Banu Lahab are expert, so do not be one who disregards the saying of a Lahabi when the birds pass.*

And to it refers the words of the author of 'Amud al-Nasab:

*Among the Madlaj ibn Bakr is qiyafah, as among the Lahab was 'iyafah.*

And he spoke truly who said:

*By your life, the casters of pebbles do not know, nor do the bird-readers, what Allah is doing.*

The reason some scholars declared disbelief for one who claims insight into the unseen is that he claimed for himself what Allah, exalted, has reserved for Himself apart from His creatures, and denied the Qur'an that reports this, such as His saying: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [al-Naml 27:65], and His saying here: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am 6:59], and the like.

From Shaykh Abu 'Imran, one of the Maliki scholars: the payment (hulwan) of the soothsayer is not lawful for him, and it is not returned to the one who gave it; rather it goes to the Muslims. This is in similar cases which some Maliki scholars put into verse, saying:

*Whatever wealth they forbade that one benefit from, its gift is forbidden and its return is prohibited.*

*The soothsayer's hulwan, the wage of singing, the wailer's pay, the bribe, and the dowry of fornication.*

(p-485) Thus it is said. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 60:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who takes your souls by night, and knows what you have committed by day﴾ – the verse. In this noble verse He mentions that sleep is a form of death (wafah). In another place He indicates that it is a lesser death (wafah sughra), that its experiencer has not actually died, and that He, may He be exalted, sends back his soul to his body until his term is fulfilled. As for the death of true dying (wafat al-mawt), which is the greater death (al-kubra), its experiencer has indeed died, and therefore He keeps his soul with Him. This is in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep. Then He withholds those on whom He has decreed death and sends the others back until a specified term. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ [al-Zumar: 42].

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And He sends over you guardians﴾, the verse. He does not state here what they guard, but He explains it in other places. He mentions that among what they guard is the human body, in His saying: ﴿For him are successive angels before him and behind him, guarding him by the command of Allah﴾ [al-Ra'd: 11]. He mentions that among what they guard is all of his deeds, good and bad, in His saying: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 10, 11, 12], and His saying: ﴿When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left. Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer ready [to record]﴾ [Qaf: 17, 18], and His saying: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private conversation? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾.

(p-277) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-An'am

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab*:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then they will be returned to God, their true Master﴾ [the verse].

This noble verse indicates that God is the Master (mawla) of the disbelievers. A parallel to it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There every soul will experience what it has sent ahead, and they will be returned to God, their true Master, and what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾ [10].

Another verse has come that indicates the opposite, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is because God is the Master of those who believe, and the disbelievers have no master﴾ [Muhammad: 11].

The answer to this is that the meaning of His being the Master of the disbelievers is that He is their Owner, who disposes of them as He wills. The meaning of His being the Master of the believers, to the exclusion of the disbelievers, is the guardianship (walaya) of love, success (tawfiq) and support. And knowledge is with God, may He be exalted.

As for the view of those who said that the pronoun in His saying "returned" and in His saying ﴿their Master﴾ refers to the angels, then there is no difficulty in the verse at all. But the first view is more apparent.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our signs, turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than that.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from sitting with those who engage in vain talk (khawd) concerning His signs. He did not explain the manner of their khawd concerning them, which is the cause for prohibiting sitting with them, nor did He mention the ruling on sitting with them here. He explained all of that in another place. He clarified that their khawd concerning them is through disbelief and mockery, by His saying: ﴿And He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of Allah being rejected and mocked, do not sit with them﴾ up to the end of the verse [An-Nisa: 140].

He also clarified that whoever sits with them at the time of their khawd concerning them is like them in sin, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them﴾. He clarified the ruling for one who sits with them forgetfully, and then reminded him by His saying here: ﴿And if Satan should make you forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-An'am: 68], as was mentioned previously in Surat An-Nisa.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 69:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there is nothing upon those who are mindful (of God) to account for the others, but it is a reminder, so that they may be mindful.﴾ This noble verse implies that there is no sin upon one who sits with those who engage in mockery and denial regarding the signs of God.

There is a verse indicating that whoever sits with them is like them in sin, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He has already revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the signs of God being denied and mocked, do not sit with them until they enter into a different conversation; otherwise, you would be like them.﴾ [al-Nisa': 140]. Know first that regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿And there is nothing upon those who are mindful (of God) to account for the others﴾ [6], there are two views among the scholars:

(p-278) The first: the meaning is that there is nothing upon those who are mindful, regarding the sitting with the disbelievers when they engage in discourse about the signs of God, to account for the disbelievers. According to this view, there is no difficulty in the verse at all.

The second view: the meaning of the verse is: there is nothing upon those who are mindful, regarding what occurs from the disbelievers of engaging in discourse about the signs of God while sitting with them, to account for it.

According to this view, the concession to sit with the disbelievers granted to the mindful believers was at the beginning of Islam, out of necessity, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you would then be like them.﴾

Among those who held that it was abrogated are Mujahid, al-Suddi, Ibn Juraij and others, as transmitted from them by Ibn Kathir. Thus it becomes clear that there is no difficulty on either view.

As for the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but it is a reminder, so that they may be mindful﴾ [6]: according to the first view, it means that if they avoid their gatherings, they are safe from sin; but the command to avoid sitting with them when they engage in discourse about the signs does not remove the obligation to remind them, admonish them, and enjoin on them the good and forbid them from the evil, so that they may perhaps be mindful of God because of that.

According to the second view, the meaning is that the concession regarding sitting does not remove the reminding, so that they may perhaps be mindful and cease engaging in discourse about the signs of God in falsehood, when the reminder is delivered to them by you. As for making the pronoun refer to the mindful, its distance is not hidden. And God knows best.

His saying: ﴿When the night covered him, he saw a star and said, "This is my lord"﴾, and the rest of the verses. His saying "This is my lord" [al-An'am: 76] in the three places is open to two possibilities. It is possible because he was supposing this, as has been related from Ibn 'Abbas and others (p-486). It is also possible because he was certain that no one other than God has lordship (rububiyyah), and his meaning was "This is my lord" according to your false claim, or he omitted the interrogative particle of denial (istifham al-inkar). The Qur'an shows the falsity of the first and the soundness of the second.

As for the falsity of the first: God denied that Abraham had ever been among the polytheists (al-mushrikin), in His saying ﴿And he was not of the polytheists﴾ [Al 'Imran: 67], in several verses. The denial of a past state covers the entire past time, so it is established that no associating of partners (shirk) preceded him at any time.

As for his being certain and sure that no one other than God has lordship, this is indicated by the sequence of His saying ﴿When the night covered him, he saw a star and said, "This is my lord"﴾, to its end, joined "with the fa'" (fa', the particle of consequence) to His saying ﴿And thus We showed Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, that he might be among the certain﴾ [al-An'am: 75]. This shows that he said that while certain, debating with them and arguing against them, as His saying indicates ﴿And his people argued with him﴾ [al-An'am: 80], and His saying ﴿And that was Our argument, which We gave to Abraham against his people﴾ [al-An'am: 83] and the verse. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 82:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ — the verse. Here, by "wrongdoing" (zulm) is meant shirk (associating partners with God), as was established from the Prophet (ﷺ) in Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him). This is clarified by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, association [with Him] is a great wrongdoing﴾ [Luqman: 13], and His saying: ﴿And it is the disbelievers who are the wrongdoers﴾ [Yusuf: 254], and His saying: ﴿And do not invoke other than Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you. For if you did, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ [Yunus: 106].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 83:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave to Abraham﴾ — the verse. Mujahid and others said that it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And how should I fear what you have associated, when you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority? So which of the two parties is more deserving of security?﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 81]. Allah confirmed him in this, and judged him to have security and guidance, saying: ﴿Those who have believed and have not mixed their belief with wrongdoing — for them there is security, and they are the ones guided﴾ [al-An'am: 82].

The apparent meaning is that it encompasses all of his arguments against them, as in His saying: ﴿I do not love the setting ones﴾ — the verse [al-An'am: 76]. This is because the setting that occurs to the star, the sun, and the moon is the greatest proof and clearest argument for the negation of lordship from them. Abraham — upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace — argued by setting, to negate lordship, in His saying: ﴿I do not love the setting ones﴾. So the omission of this argument from His saying: ﴿And that was Our argument﴾ is not apparent. Based on what we have mentioned, that the argument encompasses all of his mentioned arguments, al-Qurtubi introduced it (p. 487). And Allah knows best.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had they associated others with God, all that they used to do would have been in vain﴾. He, exalted is He, mentioned that these prophets mentioned in this noble surah, had they associated others with God, all their deeds would have been nullified.

In another place He stated explicitly that this was revealed to our Prophet (ﷺ) and to the prophets before him, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all. This is His saying: ﴿And it has been revealed to you and to those before you: If you associate others with God, your deeds will surely be lost﴾ [az-Zumar: 65]. This is a conditional (shart) statement, and a conditional statement does not imply that the condition must occur,

- like His saying: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 81], according to the view that *in* (إنْ, the conditional particle) is conditional here,

- and His saying: ﴿If We had wished to take a pastime﴾ [al-Anbiya': 17],

- and His saying: ﴿If God had wished to take a son﴾ [az-Zumar: 4].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 92:

The author said in (Dafʿ Iyhām al-Idtirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb) (Removing the Appearance of Inconsistency from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And this is a Book which We have sent down, blessed, confirming that which was before it, and that you may warn the Mother of the Cities and those around it.﴾

The ignorant person may imagine from this that his warning (ﷺ) is restricted to the Mother of the Cities and what is near it, to the exclusion of distant regions, because of His saying: ﴿and those around it.﴾ A parallel to this is His saying in Surat al-Shura: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an that you may warn the Mother of the Cities and those around it, and warn of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt.﴾ [al-Shura: 7].

Other verses have come that explicitly state the generality of his warning (ﷺ) to all people, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [25],

• His saying: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19],

• His saying: (p-279) ﴿Say, O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158],

• His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ and the verse [Saba': 28].

The answer is from two aspects:

The first: that what is meant by His saying ﴿and those around it﴾ includes the entire earth, as related by Ibn Jarir and others from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second aspect: even if we grant, for the sake of argument, that His saying ﴿and those around it﴾ includes only what is near Makkah the Honoured, which Allah made sacred, such as the Arabian Peninsula for example, the other verses explicitly state generality, such as His saying: ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾.

The mention of some individuals of a general term by way of its ruling does not restrict it according to the majority of scholars, and none dissented on this except Abu Thawr. We have already presented this clearly with its evidences in Surat al-Ma'idah.

So the verse according to this view is like His saying: ﴿And warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214], for it does not indicate the non-warning of others, as is clear. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed"﴾. That is: there is no one more unjust than the one who says, "There shall be revealed the like of what Allah has revealed." A parallel to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this"﴾ [al-Anfal: 31]. Allah, exalted is He, has made clear their lying in this fabrication of theirs, since He challenged all the Arabs with a single surah from it, as He mentioned in al-Baqarah with His saying: ﴿So bring a surah like it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 23], and in Yunus with His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring a surah like it"﴾ [Yunus: 38], and He challenged them in Hud with ten surahs like it in His saying: ﴿Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, forged"﴾, and He challenged them with the whole of it in al-Tur with His saying: ﴿Then let them bring a statement like it, if they are truthful﴾.

Then He explicitly declared in surat Bani Isra'il the incapacity of all creation to produce its like, in His saying: ﴿Say, "If mankind and the jinn gathered to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another assistants"﴾ [al-Isra': 88]. Thus the falsehood of their false claim became clear.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the angels extend their hands﴾, the verse. He did not explicitly state here the thing to which they extend their hands, but He indicated that it is punishment, by His saying: ﴿Emit your souls today; you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾, the verse [al-An'am: 93]. He declared this explicitly in His saying: ﴿If you could see when the angels take the disbelievers, striking their faces and their backs﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. And He clarified in other places that extending the hand means reaching out with harm, as in His saying: ﴿And they would extend to you their hands and their tongues with evil﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 2], and His saying: ﴿If you extend your hand toward me to kill me﴾, the verse [al-Ma'idah: 28].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 96:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He made the night a tranquility﴾, meaning: dark and still, so that creatures may rest in it and thereby be relieved of the fatigue of toil by day, as His saying, exalted is He, explains: ﴿It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight﴾ [Yunus: 67], and His saying: ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you light? Then will you not listen?"﴾ ﴿Say: "Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you may rest? Then will you not see?"﴾ ﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty﴾ [al-Qasas: 71, 72, 73]. And His saying: ﴿that you may rest therein﴾ refers to the night, and ﴿and seek of His bounty﴾ refers to the day. ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day﴾ [Fussilat: 37], the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾. The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that the wisdom behind the creation of the stars is solely guidance by them,

• like His saying: ﴿And by the star they are guided﴾ [al-Nahl: 16], but He, exalted is He, has explained in another place that they have two other wisdoms besides guidance by them; namely, adorning the lowest heaven and pelting the devils with them,

• like His saying: ﴿And We have certainly adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5], to the end of the verse,

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars﴾ ﴿and as protection from every rebellious devil﴾ ﴿They cannot listen to the Exalted Assembly and are pelted from every side﴾ ﴿driven away, and for them is a constant punishment﴾ ﴿except one who snatches a fragment, so he is pursued by a piercing flame﴾ [al-Saffat: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10],

• and His saying: ﴿And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 98:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced you from a single soul, and [for you is] a place of storage and a place of rest﴾, the verse. He did not explain here the manner of their being produced from a single soul. However, He explained in other places that its manner is that He created from that single one, who is Adam, his spouse Hawwa' (Eve), and dispersed from the two of them many men and women, as in His saying: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from the two of them many men and women﴾ [an-Nisa': 1], and His saying: ﴿It is He who created you from a single soul and made from it its mate that it might find tranquillity in her﴾, the verse [al-A'raf: 189].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 99:

The author said in (Dafʿ Iyhām al-Iḍṭirāb ʿan Āyāt al-Kitāb, "Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book"):

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾.

And His statement also: ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾ [al-An'am: 141]. In these two verses He affirmed similarity for the olive and the pomegranate and negated it of them.

The answer is what Qatadah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: that the meaning is that they are similar in their leaves but differ in their taste. And Allah knows best.

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 103:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا تُدْرِكُهُ الأبْصارُ﴾ الآيَةَ، أشارَ في مَواضِعَ أُخَرَ إلى أنَّ نَفْيَ الإدْراكِ المَذْكُورِ هُنا لا يَقْتَضِي نَفْيَ مُطْلَقِ الرُّؤْيَةِ،

• كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ﴾ ﴿إلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ﴾ [القيامة: ٢٢، ٢٣]،

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا الحُسْنى وزِيادَةٌ﴾ [يونس: ٢٦]، والحُسْنى الجَنَّةُ، والزِّيادَةُ النَّظَرُ إلى وجْهِ اللَّهِ الكَرِيمِ،

• وقَوْلِهِ: ﴿كَلّا إنَّهم عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ﴾ [المطففين: ١٥]،

يُفْهَمُ مِنهُ أنَّ المُؤْمِنِينَ لَيْسُوا مَحْجُوبِينَ عَنْهُ، وهو كَذَلِكَ.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾ and so on. This noble verse gives the impression that Allah, exalted is He, cannot be seen with the eyes. Yet other verses indicate that He can be seen with the eyes, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22-23], and His saying: ﴿For those who did good is the best (reward) and more﴾ [Yunus: 26]. The "best" (al-husna) is Paradise, and the "more" (al-ziyadah) is looking at the Noble Face of Allah. Likewise His saying: ﴿They will have whatever they wish therein, and with Us is more﴾ [Qaf: 35], according to one of the two opinions. And His saying about the disbelievers: ﴿Nay, indeed they, that Day, will be veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15]. From the implication of its address (dalil khitabihi, the reasoning drawn from what is said by contrast) it is understood that the believers will not be veiled from their Lord.

The answer has three aspects:

The first: the meaning of ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾ is "in this world", so it does not contradict seeing Him in the Hereafter.

The second: it is a general statement specified by the believers' seeing Him in the Hereafter. This is close in meaning to the first.

The third, which is the truth: what is negated in this verse is comprehension that implies encompassing His essence (al-kunh). As for seeing in general, the verse does not indicate its negation. Rather it is established by these Qur'anic verses, by the sound hadiths, and by the agreement of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah).

The summary of this answer: comprehension (al-idrak) is more specific than seeing in general, because the comprehension meant is encompassing. The Arabs say: "I saw the thing but did not comprehend it (ma adraktuhu)." So the meaning of ﴿No vision comprehends Him﴾ is that vision does not encompass Him, just as creatures know Him but do not encompass Him in knowledge.

Sane people have agreed that negating the more specific does not necessitate negating the more general. So the absence of comprehension does not entail the absence of seeing in general, even though no one among creation comprehends His true essence.

The evidence for the soundness of this aspect is what al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related from the hadith of Abu Musa, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "His veil is light, or fire. Were He to remove it, the glories of His Face would burn away whatever of His creation His sight reaches."

The hadith is explicit that He is not seen in this world, and from it is understood the impossibility of encompassing Him absolutely.

The conclusion: His being seen with the eyes is rationally possible in this world and the Hereafter, because every existing thing may rationally be seen. The rational possibility is shown by Musa's words: ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself that I may look at You﴾ [al-A'raf: 143], since he would not be ignorant of what is rationally possible with respect to Allah, exalted is He.

As for the revealed law (al-shar'), it is permissible and will occur in the Hereafter, but is impossible in this world. Among the clearest evidences for this is what Muslim and Ibn Khuzaymah related, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed you will not see your Lord until you die." The hadiths about the believers seeing Him on the Day of Resurrection are widely transmitted (mutawatir). And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 6, verse 105:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that they may say, "You have studied"﴾, the verse, meaning: that they may claim that the Prophet ﷺ learned this Qur'an through study and instruction from someone else among the People of the Book, just as the disbelievers of Makkah claimed that he ﷺ learned this Qur'an from Jabr and Yasar, who were two Christian slaves in Makkah. Allah, exalted is He, has made clear the falsehood of their fabrication in this matter in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human who teaches him." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, but this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ [An-Nahl: 103],

• and His saying: ﴿So he reflected and calculated. Then he was killed; how he calculated! Then he considered. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned back and was arrogant. And he said, "This is not but magic transmitted. This is not but the word of a human." I will burn him in Saqar﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 24, 25, 26], and the meaning of "yu'thar" (transmitted) is: Muhammad ﷺ narrates it from someone else, according to their false claim,

• and His saying: (p-490) ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "This is not but a falsehood he has invented, and other people have helped him at it." So they have certainly committed an injustice and a falsehood. And they say, "Tales of the former peoples, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." Say, "It has been sent down by He who knows the secret within the heavens and the earth"﴾, the verse [Al-Furqan: 4, 5, 6],

and to other verses besides these.

In His saying: ﴿dartast﴾ [Al-An'am: 105], there are three canonical readings:

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it as "dārasta" with an alif after the dal, with the sin sukun and the ta' fathah, from the form of mufa'alah, meaning: you studied with the People of the Book and they studied with you, until you acquired this knowledge.

The rest of the Seven, other than Ibn 'Amir, read it as "darasta" without the alif, with the sin sukun and the ta' also fathah, meaning: you studied this with the People of the Book until you learned it from them.

Ibn 'Amir read it as "darasta" with fathah on the dal, the ra' and the sin, and the ta' sukun, taking it as the ta' of feminine marking, with the subject being a pronoun referring back to the verses mentioned in His saying: ﴿And thus We detail the verses﴾ [Al-An'am: 105].

Al-Qurtubi said: The best that has been said regarding the reading of Ibn 'Amir is that the meaning is: "and lest they say, 'They have ceased and been erased,' and Muhammad ﷺ does not bring anything other than them." End of quote.

Al-Qurtubi also said: ﴿And that they may say, "You have studied"﴾: the waw is for coordination with an implied element, meaning: We detail the verses so that the proof may be established, ﴿and that they may say, "You have studied"﴾. It was also said: ﴿and that they may say, "You have studied"﴾ means: We turned them away.

The one who restricts this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: Both meanings return to one thing, and the Qur'an bears witness to this in many verses, indicating that it makes the truth clear in this Book, so that it guides with it some people and makes it a proof against others,

• such as His saying: ﴿So that you may give good news with it to the righteous and warn with it a people who are stubborn in opposition﴾ [Maryam: 97],

• and His saying: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is for them a blindness"﴾ [Fussilat: 44],

• and His saying: ﴿So that those who were given the Scripture may be certain and those who believe may increase in faith, and those who were given the Scripture and the believers will not doubt, and so that those in whose hearts is disease and the disbelievers will say, "What did Allah intend by this as an example?" Thus Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 31],

as He said here: ﴿and that they may say, "You have studied," and that We may make it clear to a people who know﴾. So the wretched say, "You learned it from a human through study," while the people of knowledge and the blessed know that it is the truth about which there is no doubt.

The author said in *Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab* (Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, the verse.
